name: Identify shapes within a composite shape
description: Student can identify the familiar shapes that make up a composite shape.
exampleOfSuccess: In a house drawing, the student identifies the square and the triangle.
commonError: Student names the whole figure without breaking it into parts.
checkpointTask: Show composite shapes. Ask the student to identify the familiar shapes in each.

name: Make a composite shape from parts
description: Student can make a composite shape by combining familiar shapes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student combines two triangles to make a rectangle.
commonError: Student overlaps shapes or leaves gaps when combining.
checkpointTask: Give familiar shapes. Ask the student to combine them to make a named composite shape.

name: Approximate a real object with shapes
description: Student can approximate a complex object using combinations of familiar shapes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student represents a tree as a triangle on a rectangle.
commonError: Student uses one shape that does not capture the object.
checkpointTask: Show real objects. Ask the student to approximate each with familiar shapes.

name: Build a 3D model from cubes
description: Student can build a three-dimensional model that approximates a real object using cubes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student builds a model of a chair from connecting cubes.
commonError: Student builds a flat arrangement rather than a 3D model.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to build a cube model that approximates a real object.

name: Read a grid reference
description: Student can read a grid reference to find a location.
exampleOfSuccess: On a grid map, the student finds the item at B3.
commonError: Student reverses the column and row, or counts the lines instead of the cells.
checkpointTask: Give a grid map. Ask the student to find items at named grid references.

name: Give the grid reference for a location
description: Student can give the grid reference for a location on a map.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the treasure is at D2.
commonError: Student gives the reference in the wrong order.
checkpointTask: Give a grid map. Ask the student to name the grid reference for marked items.

name: Describe a pathway using grid references
description: Student can describe a pathway between locations using grid references and directions.
exampleOfSuccess: The student describes a route from A1 to C3 using moves and references.
commonError: Student describes a path that does not connect the start and end.
checkpointTask: Give a grid map. Ask the student to describe a route between two points.

name: Create a grid reference map
description: Student can create a grid reference system on a map of a familiar space.
exampleOfSuccess: The student adds a labelled grid to a map and places landmarks.
commonError: Student labels the grid inconsistently so references do not work.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to add a grid reference system to a map and place landmarks.

name: Identify line symmetry
description: Student can identify whether a shape has line symmetry.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a square has line symmetry and a scalene triangle does not.
commonError: Student calls any shape symmetrical, or misjudges the fold line.
checkpointTask: Show shapes. Ask the student which have line symmetry.

name: Find the lines of symmetry
description: Student can find all the lines of symmetry of a shape.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds four lines of symmetry on a square.
commonError: Student finds only the obvious vertical line and misses the others.
checkpointTask: Give shapes. Ask the student to draw all the lines of symmetry.

name: Identify rotational symmetry
description: Student can identify whether a shape has rotational symmetry.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a windmill shape looks the same as it turns, so it has rotational symmetry.
commonError: Student confuses rotational symmetry with line symmetry.
checkpointTask: Show shapes. Ask the student which have rotational symmetry.

name: Create a symmetrical pattern
description: Student can create a symmetrical pattern or picture.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a pattern with a line of symmetry down the middle.
commonError: Student makes a pattern that is not actually symmetrical.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to create a pattern with line or rotational symmetry.
